claims.title: Dual evaluation of a nonzero compact-weight intertwiner
claims.hypotheses: The definite unitary representation has odd rank, a nonzero finite part at weight W and a prescribed cuspidal type at a good split place.
claims.statement: Evaluation produces a nonzero function on finite unitary arguments valued in the algebraic dual of the compact weight. Its rational covariance and its finite level come from the original intertwiner.

claims.title: Extension to similitudes and selection of a central eigenvector
claims.hypotheses: The multiplier-one function obeys rational covariance and has the prescribed type and spherical eigenvalues. The central norm map is continuous and sends principal ideles to rational scalars.
claims.statement: Extension by zero yields a nonzero similitude form. Its central translates span a finite-dimensional subspace of the common eigenspace for the observed operators. This subspace contains a central eigenform.

claims.title: The central similitude from a conjugated relative norm
claims.hypotheses: E is a CM field containing the imaginary quadratic subfield K generated by x. Use normalized valuations. The norm comparison for uniformizers assumes the two restrictions of the place to K are distinct.
claims.statement: The conjugated relative norm and the absolute norm form a central similitude. For a local argument its scalar support lies above the conjugate place of K. Its valuation is the residue degree multiplied by the extension ramification index and by the input valuation.

claims.title: The algebraic Hecke character and its local inverse
claims.hypotheses: The central map and the rational coefficient action are fixed. The nonzero form has central eigencharacter ψ on the finite ideles, and the preimage of the character-kernel level is open. The uniformizer test excludes the level and the conjugate self-restriction.
claims.statement: Multiplying the inverse finite character by the archimedean monomial gives a character on the idele classes. Its inverse local uniformizer value gives the right-translation scalar used in an observed spherical test.

claims.title: Choosing the geometric prime after a nonzero value
claims.hypotheses: The original central eigenform has finite level support. The geometric prime construction can exclude a prescribed finite set in addition to satisfying the reduction and observation conditions.
claims.statement: One geometric prime avoids the original level and the denominators of the chosen nonzero argument and its inverse. This supplies both requirements for retaining a nonzero value through the frame.
